phase_0.boundary_condition: The merged graph structure where n cliques of size n share at most one vertex, creating a topological obstruction to n-coloring.

⊢.justification: The state before any vertices or edges are defined, representing the void from which the n cliques will be constructed.

⊣.justification: The closed system containing all n cliques and their intersections, defining the scope of the coloring problem.

≻.justification: The forward morphism building each of the n cliques with n vertices, establishing the local complete subgraphs.

≺.justification: The reverse morphism representing the descent into the state where n colors are insufficient, tracing the conflict back to the intersection constraints.

⋈.justification: The sequential composition of merging vertices and edges from individual cliques into the single global graph structure.

⊙.justification: The identity of the merged graph recognizing its own structural rigidity and the impossibility of n-coloring within its own definition.

∈.justification: The split into two branches: one attempting a valid n-coloring (T-arm) and one encountering a conflict (F-arm) due to the intersection topology.

∋.justification: The rejoining of the coloring attempt and conflict branches into a single state where the graph requires n+1 colors, fusing the success and failure into a B-state of structural necessity.

⊤.justification: The affirmative state where each individual clique is successfully colored with n colors in isolation.

⊥.justification: The negative state where the merged graph fails to be colored with n colors due to shared vertices forcing color collisions.

⊞.justification: The paradice state holding both the local validity of cliques and the global failure of the merged graph simultaneously, representing the topological obstruction.

⊡.justification: The permanent record that the chromatic number of the merged graph exceeds n, fixing the result of the topological analysis.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the empty graph state before any cliques are defined.
Construct the first clique with n vertices.
Merge the first clique into the growing graph structure.
Construct the second clique with n vertices.
Merge the second clique, ensuring at most one shared vertex with the first.
Construct the third clique with n vertices.
Merge the third clique, maintaining the intersection constraint.
Continue merging all n cliques into the single graph.
The merged graph recognizes its own structure and intersection topology.
Branch into a coloring attempt (T-arm) and a conflict check (F-arm).
Affirm that each individual clique can be colored with n colors.
Propagate the coloring attempt across the merged graph.
Detect the conflict where shared vertices force a color collision.
Trace the conflict back to the intersection constraints of the cliques.
Hold the state where local validity and global conflict coexist.
Rejoin the branches to form the verdict that the graph requires n+1 colors.
Record the chromatic number as exceeding n permanently.
Close the system with the final merged graph and its chromatic property.
